name: CoreConnectV3
intent: Core Connect V3: V2's merged workspace re-cut around the project lifecycle. The sidebar keeps a pinned Home with the installed apps directly beneath it, but replaces V2's single "Your apps" heading with one labelled group per lifecycle stage — Design, Plan, Capture, Pay — each carrying an icon that stands for the whole stage: collapsed, the rail shows the four group icons instead of every app, and clicking one opens a flyout of the apps under it, reusing the same drill-in an expandable nav item already has. Each stage header carries two distinct targets: its name opens a page about that stage (its purpose, the apps installed under it, and what else the Marketplace offers for it), and a chevron on the far right folds those apps away. The workspace opens as a project already kitted out, with nine of the thirteen catalogue apps installed across the four stages, and the rest available to add from the Marketplace, where anything can also be uninstalled. The Marketplace moves out of the shell's pinned slot and becomes the last item of the Studio group, so browsing and installing apps reads as studio work rather than a permanent fixture. The top-bar switcher moves up a rung with it: where V1 and V2 pick a project there, V3 picks the ORGANIZATION, since the rail beneath it is already cut by project lifecycle and the project is chosen further in. The project is chosen in Files, the other thing V3 adds: one flat list, reached from a Files entry pinned under the nav search and ruled off from Home and the app stages below it, of every record the workspace holds in the selected organization, each carrying its folder path. Facets down the left — type, project and tag, each with a count — narrow it; there is no folder tree, because the folder is already printed under every row and a facet answers “show me the pipelines” in one click where a tree cannot. Opening a file navigates to the app that owns it and drills to that record; every app listing shows, beside each record, the folder it lives in, and clicking that reopens Files narrowed to it. The file system is a reference layer with no records of its own. Every other surface, and the install lifecycle behind it, is unchanged from V2.
when: Organising a Connect sidebar by project lifecycle stage rather than one undifferentiated app list
A shell where browsing the app catalogue belongs inside the admin studio rather than pinned to the frame
Demonstrating a workspace that opens already kitted out, rather than an empty first-run shell
A sidebar whose sections must stay navigable when collapsed, one icon per section rather than a long undifferentiated icon run
A shell scoped by organization in the top bar, with the project chosen further in rather than in the frame
A workspace where every record needs an address — browsing pipelines, processes and ontology types by folder rather than only through the perspective that owns each one
whenNot: The flat "Your apps" list with Marketplace pinned to the shell -> use CoreConnect (V2)
The V1 two-portal split, where the admin side stands alone -> use WC3 Workspace
The V1 end-user portal, where the marketplace IS the whole app -> use AppInstaller

chooseOver.because: CoreConnect is the V2 cut: one "Your apps" list and a Marketplace pinned to the shell. V3 groups the same apps by lifecycle stage and folds Marketplace into Studio.
AppInstaller is the V1 end-user portal, where the store is the entire app. V3 keeps the same store as one Studio surface beside the admin perspectives.

allowedPlacement: route-level workspace surface that owns the full window

extracted: every surface and the install lifecycle, unchanged — V3 differs only in how the rail is organised
the lifecycle stage per app from APP_LIFECYCLE in app-marketplace-shared.tsx
the Studio group and pinned Home from the same CoreWC3Workspace merged mode V2 uses

lineage.confidence: unset — prototype, no held-out eval yet
notes: pilot: true

Implemented as CoreWC3Workspace with `withMarketplace`, `appGrouping="lifecycle"`, `marketplacePlacement="studio"`, `switcherScope="organization"` and `showFiles` — a thin alias, not a fork, so V2 and V3 cannot drift
The Design / Plan / Capture / Pay placement of each app is provisional nav metadata, not behaviour; moving an app between stages is a one-line edit in APP_LIFECYCLE
Opens with CONNECT_STARTER_APPS installed so all four lifecycle sections are populated; a section disappears only if everything under it is uninstalled
Preinstalled apps carry no green "new" dot — that marks something the user just added — but are otherwise ordinary installs that can be removed and re-added
App catalog is sample data; install/uninstall is local state only and resets on reload

Landed alongside a CoreAppSidebar addition: SidebarNavGroup gained an optional `icon`, which shows beside the label expanded and collapses the group to a single rail icon with a flyout. The flyout is the SAME component an expandable item's subMenu uses, so group and item drill-in cannot diverge
Groups without an icon are untouched — every other template keeps rendering each item as its own rail icon

SidebarNavGroup also gained `collapsible` (a chevron that folds the group) and `id` (making the name a link that fires onGroupSelect). Both are opt-in, so no existing template grows an affordance it did not ask for

Studio is a group on the same footing as the four stages: same clickable name, same chevron. Its page is the perspective-card HomeView the standalone workspace already lands on, which merged mode otherwise has no use for since its Home is the app launcher
Studio carries a group icon like the stages do, so the collapsed rail is uniformly one icon per group: Home, the four stages, then Studio, whose flyout holds the perspectives and Marketplace
Studio sets `dividerBefore` so the rail keeps the break between the app stages and the admin section — consecutive icon-groups otherwise run together, which would read as one undifferentiated list
Home takes a divider below it here (unlike V2, where Home runs straight into its "Your apps" list): every section in this rail is named, so Home is a section of its own
The sidebar find bar is enabled; a live query forces folded groups open so a match cannot hide behind a collapsed header

An expanded icon-group renders as a tree: the header is a parent row at item size (not the small uppercase caption), and its items hang off a vertical spine — aligned to the group icon's centre, starting below the icon, stopping at the last item — with an elbow branching into each item at its vertical middle. Items are indented so their own icons clear the spine
Groups without an icon are untouched by all of it: they keep the small uppercase caption and a plain item list, which is why V1, V2 and every other template on this sidebar look exactly as before

Files is the FileSystem WIDGET, not template code: the surface shipped here first and was lifted to packages/components/src/file-system once it was clear nothing in it was Core-specific. The template supplies the nodes, declares its own file types, and reads the opaque `ref` a file carries; the widget holds no data and knows no product. What stays here is the adapter — wc3-fs-data.ts (the fixture), wc3-fs-store.ts (the live array and the reverse lookup five perspectives read for their Location column), wc3-fs-types.tsx (the type registry) and wc3-fs-records.ts (the record constructors)

The surface is FACETED, not hierarchical: one flat list of files with type / project / tag facets down the left. A folder tree was built first (on @headless-tree) and removed — it repeated the path already printed under every row, cost the widest column on the surface, and could not answer the question the list is actually asked. Rows are PROJECTS and files, and a row never navigates: clicking one selects it and a details panel answers “what is this?”, while the underlined NAME is the only thing that leaves — a file's name opens the app that owns it, a project's name swaps the layout for that project's own page (Overview / Files / Trash down the left). A plain folder is not a row — the folder a file is in is already printed under its name. Folders survive as `folderId`, which is what a Location link in another app applies; the tree dependency went with the tree

Tags INHERIT: a file matches its own tags plus every tag on the project and folders above it, so a project tagged “riyadh” makes its files findable under it. Facet counts and query matches come from the same function, so the rail can never offer a value that finds nothing

`openWorkspaceTarget`'s `recordId` stopped being decorative with this change: it is handed to the arriving view as `openRecordId` and consumed once, so a file opens its record rather than the tab that contains it. Pipelines, Processes, Products, object types and action types accept it; the remaining tabs ignore it harmlessly

The inbound half is `Wc3FsPathLabel`, a Location column (and card line) on every listing whose records are addressed. It renders nothing for a record with no address — an empty cell is honest, a "/" would claim a root the record is not in
Files that reference nothing — a dataset, a write-up — are ordinary tree citizens: they render, filter and search, and clicking one does not navigate, because no app owns them

The top-bar switcher is scoped by `switcherScope`: V1/V2 leave it on projects, V3 sets `organization`. Only the list, the selection and the switcher's own copy change — no surface below the bar is filtered by it yet, and each scope persists under its own key so the two selections never overwrite each other
Navigate and fold are deliberately SEPARATE targets in one header row, not one click that does both; a search forces every group open so a match can never hide behind a folded header
